stem: Which of the following properties of the glomerular capillary wall most selectively restricts negatively charged plasma proteins?

options.label: A
options.text: Fenestrations in the capillary endothelium that admit only cells, not fluid
options.misconception: Endothelial fenestrae are being described as cell-only pores.
options.explanation: Fenestrae allow plasma fluid and small solutes; charge selectivity against proteins comes mainly from negatively charged barrier elements.

options.label: B
options.text: Fixed negative charges on the capillary wall
options.misconception: None; anionic barrier charges repel anionic proteins such as albumin.
options.explanation: The glomerular barrier carries fixed negative charges that electrostatically restrict passage of negatively charged plasma proteins while permitting water and small solutes.

options.label: C
options.text: Positive charges that attract albumin into the filtrate
options.misconception: The barrier polarity is being reversed.
options.explanation: A positively charged barrier would favor albumin filtration; the real barrier is anionic and restricts albumin.

options.label: D
options.text: Active tubular secretion of albumin in the PCT
options.misconception: A tubular process is being substituted for glomerular restriction.
options.explanation: Albumin is normally kept out of the filtrate by the glomerular barrier; PCT handling is not the primary charge-selective gate.

options.label: E
options.text: Ureteral peristalsis that returns protein to plasma
options.misconception: Downstream conduit motility is being invented as a filtration mechanism.
options.explanation: Ureteral peristalsis moves urine; charge-selective exclusion of proteins occurs at the glomerular filtration barrier.

context: Learning objective: state charge selectivity of the glomerular barrier. Fixed negative charges restrict anionic plasma proteins (e.g. albumin) while water and small solutes pass.
